questions.note: Order reads right in the front view: hallux longest, toe 2 several mm short (toes 3-5 are context). Shaping fails a specialist: hallux pulp plugged on at a ringed IP crease, boxy pads and no base sulcus from below, a sleeve-cuff step under toe 2, stamped knuckle wrinkles, a knife-cut DIP, a flat-shelf web. By eye: hallux ~31 mm wide, ~20-21 mm deep at the IP; toe 2 ~15.5 mm.

By eye the hallux plate is ~19.5 mm wide (front, 21.7 px/mm) and its free edge ~1.1 mm thick (lateral zoom, 89 px/mm); the pink bed now shows through and the edges are trimmed straight. But both nails are press-ons: even gutter and gasket rim, exposed margins, near-flat plates, constant-width glassy French-tip edges, no hallux lunula, no cuticle; toe 2's plate ~10 mm vs 11.

Within scope nothing reads: no EHL cord over the first MTP or along the hallux's proximal phalanx (front and medial silhouettes are smooth there), no extensor slip on toe 2, no dorsal veins. Faint soft ridges toward toes 3-4 are relief, not paint, but die out before the MTPs. The saphenous vein is not in frame.

Shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows, so the SSS is believable. The micro-relief is wrong: one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle everywhere (cells 0.4-0.8 mm on toe 2 and the web at 98 px/mm, against 0.25-0.4), corduroy ridges at one angle over ball and pads, no pores, no dorsal-to-volar change at the tips. Colour and sheen not judged (declared first pass).

defects.what: Under toe 2 a crisp straight ledge rings the toe: the distal part steps out like a sleeve cuff, with small flaps poking past the silhouette at both ends, smooth skin above and ridged below. A seam that no toe has.
defects.fix: Make the skin one continuous surface: a plantar flexion crease is a soft infold about 0.5 mm deep that fades out on the sides, with the ridges carrying on across it.

defects.what: In profile the hallux pulp looks plugged on: the plantar outline drops in a hard V-notch at the IP crease and the groove carries on up the medial side as a ring, so the distal segment reads as a separate tube.
defects.fix: Under a resting hallux the outline arches smoothly from the base sulcus to the pulp; the plantar IP crease is a deep soft fold that shallows and ends on the medial and lateral sides.

defects.what: The hallux nail is still a press-on: a rounded-rectangle tile set in an even gutter with a thin raised gasket rim all round, its lateral margins fully exposed, its surface nearly flat across instead of falling away into the folds.
defects.fix: The lateral folds overlap and hide the plate margins, the proximal fold is a broad soft lip whose cuticle lies on the plate with no gutter, and the plate curves clearly down to both sides (11 mm radius; toe 2 6 mm).

defects.what: The hallux and toe 2 free edges are glossy bands of constant width, clear to milky like an acrylic French tip; at 89 px/mm the hallux edge is a polished grey glass slab about 1.1 mm thick.
defects.fix: A clipped toenail edge is opaque ivory keratin with air beneath, slightly uneven in width, its cut face matte and a little frayed, often with a faint grey grime line under it.

defects.what: The 1-2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin about 8 mm long that meets toe 2's medial wall at a right angle: a flat shelf between the toes. The same straight edge shows in pair_hr.hallux_eval.png and the front view.
defects.fix: A real web is a soft U-shaped saddle: the dorsal skin rolls over a rounded free margin that dips between the toe bases and curves up into each toe's side with no corner.

defects.what: From below the hallux pad is a rounded box with straight parallel sides, capped by a raised rim along its IP crease; toe 2's pad is the same box.
defects.fix: A toe pulp is an oval dome, widest distally, that rolls into the toe's sides; the IP crease is a soft fold, not a lip.

defects.what: From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball with no toe-base sulcus; its only crease is at the IP, so the toe has no root.
defects.fix: Fold the sole deeply where the hallux pad meets the ball under the first MTP: a curved crease 1-2 mm deep with the toe's pad bulging distal to it.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp each: three or four identical, evenly spaced concentric arcs with glossy lips, proud enough to saw-tooth the dorsal profile in the medial view.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin carries a loose, irregular cluster of fine creases of unequal length and depth, some branching or crossing, fading at the sides and barely touching the silhouette at rest.

defects.what: A single thin, raised, glossy line arcs about 15 mm across the first MTP dorsum and notches the profile in the medial view: it reads as a healed incision, not a skin crease.
defects.fix: Dorsal MTP skin shows at most a few faint, broken transverse creases of differing length, recessed rather than raised, with no gloss of their own.

defects.what: All skin wears one Voronoi crackle: dark-outlined polygonal cells about 0.4-0.8 mm, equally sharp on dorsum, pulp, folds and web; at native size toe 2 reads as crazed glaze.
defects.fix: Toe skin shows a faint rhomboid furrow network 0.25-0.4 mm made by shading, not dark lines, oriented along tension lines, turning into ridges on the pads and fine stretch lines on the web.

defects.what: Friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one diagonal angle across the ball and both pads, running through the creases like corduroy; the hallux pulp has no whorl or loop.
defects.fix: Each toe pad carries a whorl or loop centred on its dome, the ridges curving round it and broken at the flexion creases; on the ball they sweep in broad curves.

defects.what: No extensor hallucis longus cord rises over the first MTP or runs onto the hallux, no slip runs onto toe 2 and no dorsal vein shows: the forefoot dorsum is mannequin-smooth.
defects.fix: On a lean 40-year-old the EHL stands as a cord about 4-5 mm wide over the first MTP and along the proximal phalanx, the slip to toe 2 as a low ridge, with soft vein relief between.

defects.what: No lunula on the hallux: the plate is one translucent pink-beige from the proximal fold to the onychodermal band, with no paler crescent at its root.
defects.fix: Show a whitish crescent about 3.5 mm deep emerging from under the proximal fold, its distal edge soft.

defects.what: The hallux and toe 2 are bald: no dark hairs on the hallux's proximal phalanx or on toe 2, which reads young and groomed beside the anchor feet.
defects.fix: Give the hallux a tuft of 8-12 dark brown hairs 5-8 mm long lying flat distally, and toe 2 two to four shorter ones.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even groove with a bright lip across nearly the whole width of the toe, like a knife cut.
defects.fix: A DIP dorsum shows two or three short, soft, uneven creases that fade out before the sides.

defects.what: The hallux plate's highlight breaks into saw-toothed longitudinal flames, a brushed-metal comb; toe 2's highlights are striated bands.
defects.fix: Fine 0.25 mm ridges only ripple a highlight's edge faintly; the specular should be broad and smooth with a slight waviness.

defects.what: Just proximal to the free edge the plate carries two or three crisp, parallel white stripes, like layers of lacquer, instead of one soft onychodermal band.
defects.fix: The onychodermal band is a single narrow, slightly irregular band, pinkish-brown to whitish, where the plate leaves the bed.

defects.what: From below, glassy specks of the hallux free edge's corners glint past the pulp, and toe 2's free edge shows as a clear glass crescent beyond its tip with small spikes along its side.
defects.fix: Where a free edge shows past the pulp it is a thin opaque ivory line; usually the pulp hides it.

defects.what: In clay a tiny bright fleck sits in the hollow under the hallux free edge, as if the plate's underside breaks through the hyponychium.
defects.fix: Keep the plate's underside clear of the hyponychium, which seals onto it with a small soft fillet.

defects.what: A thin pale fin stands up where the flat web shelf meets toe 2's medial wall.
defects.fix: The web's dorsal skin rolls smoothly into toe 2's side with no fin or pinch.

defects.what: Tiny white dashes about 0.1 mm long are scattered over the toe and web skin, reading as lint or dandruff rather than pores or hair.
defects.fix: Drop them, or make them what they stand for: dark follicle openings, or dark hairs of real length.

defects.what: A tiny bright tick at the proximal medial corner of toe 2's plate suggests the plate pokes through the proximal fold there.
defects.fix: Tuck the plate's proximal corners under the fold so the eponychium covers them.

ranked: [D1] Under toe 2 a crisp ledge rings the toe and the distal part steps out like a sleeve cuff with flaps at its ends, smooth above and ridged below: a thimble glued on. Plantar creases are soft infolds that fade at the sides; the skin never steps.

[D2] The hallux's distal segment looks plugged on: in profile the plantar outline drops in a hard V-notch at the IP crease and the groove rings the medial side. A real hallux arches smoothly from base sulcus to pulp, its IP crease dying out on the sides.

[D3] The nails read as press-ons: the hallux plate is a rounded-rectangle tile in an even gutter with a gasket rim all round, margins exposed, nearly flat across. Real lateral folds swallow the margins and the plate falls away into them.

[D4] The free edges are constant-width glossy bands, clear to milky, like an acrylic French tip; up close the hallux edge is polished grey glass. A clipped toenail edge is opaque ivory keratin, uneven, matte at the cut, often with grime under it.
[D5] The 1-2 web ends in a ruler-straight horizontal margin meeting toe 2's wall at a right angle, a shelf between the toes, where a real web is a soft U-shaped saddle dipping between the toe bases.

[D6] From below the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded boxes with straight sides, the hallux pad capped by a raised rim at its IP crease; real pulps are oval domes, widest distally, rolling into the sides of the toe.
[D7] The hallux grows straight out of the ball with no toe-base sulcus underneath, so it has no root; a real sole folds deeply where the toe pad meets the ball.

[D8] Knuckle wrinkles are one stamp per joint: three or four identical concentric arcs, evenly spaced and glossy-lipped, saw-toothing the profile like bellows. Real knuckle skin has an irregular cluster of fine creases of unequal length.
[D9] A thin raised glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum and notches the medial profile; a podiatrist reads a healed incision, not a crease.

[D10] All skin wears one dark-outlined Voronoi crackle, too coarse on toe 2 and the web and the same on dorsum, pulp and fold: crazed glaze at native size, where real skin shows a faint shaded furrow network.
[D11] Friction ridges are straight parallel diagonal stripes over the ball and both pads, ignoring the creases: corduroy. A hallux pulp carries a whorl or loop centred on the pad.
[D12] No EHL cord rises over the first MTP or runs onto the hallux, no extensor slip onto toe 2, no dorsal vein: a lean soldier's forefoot would show them as low relief.
[D13] No lunula on the hallux: the plate is one translucent pink-beige from fold to onychodermal band.
[D14] The hallux and toe 2 are bald; a 40-year-old man's big toe usually carries a few dark hairs on its proximal phalanx, as the anchor feet do.
[D15] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long even groove with a bright lip across nearly the whole toe, a knife cut rather than two or three short soft creases.

In plan toe 2 is still close to a parallel-sided tube from DIP to tip: the PIP hump now reads, but the waist over the middle phalanx and the pulp flare are each only about 1-1.5 mm (toe2 view, 47.6 px/mm).
The hallux is about 31 mm wide (plantar view) but only about 20-21 mm deep at the IP (medial view, 17.9 px/mm), so in profile it reads flat and spatulate rather than a round pad.

Everything reads too clean and young for a boot-wearing 40-year-old: no cuticle on the plates, no dry or flaking skin at the folds, no yellowing or thickening of the hallux nail, no grime under the free edges.
[D16] Nail highlights break into saw-toothed longitudinal flames on the hallux and striated bands on toe 2: brushed metal rather than a smooth plate with a faint ripple.
[D17] Above the hallux free edge two or three crisp parallel white stripes read as lacquer layers, not one soft onychodermal band.
[D18] From below, glassy specks of the hallux free edge glint past the pulp and toe 2's free edge shows as a clear glass crescent beyond its tip.
[D19] In clay a bright fleck sits in the hollow under the hallux free edge, as if the plate's underside breaks through the hyponychium.
[D22] A tiny bright tick at the proximal corner of toe 2's plate suggests the plate pokes through its proximal fold.
[D20] A thin pale fin stands where the web shelf meets toe 2's medial wall.
[D21] Tiny white dashes about 0.1 mm long are scattered over the toe and web skin, like lint.
